nodes.title: Continuous Turán numbers of planar patterns
Convex and general position of point sets

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a finite-dimensional real normed space and let $L \subseteq E$ be a $\mathbb{Z}$-submodule (an additive subgroup) that is discrete in the subspace topology. Then the $\mathbb{Z}$-rank of $L$ equals $\dim_{\mathbb{R}} E$ if and only if $L$ is a $\mathbb{Z}$-lattice in $E$, that is, $L$ spans $E$ over $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: A discrete subgroup is a lattice iff it has full rank
Equilateral triangles in planar point sets

nodes.summary: An infinite set of points in the plane with pairwise integer distances is collinear.
nodes.title: Erdős–Anning theorem

nodes.summary: Let $V$, $E$ and $F$ be finite sets, let $\iota : V \to \mathbb{R}^3$ be an injective map into Euclidean space, and let $P = \operatorname{conv} \iota(V)$ be the convex hull of its image; assume $P$ has nonempty interior $\operatorname{int} P$, and write $\partial P$ for its frontier. Each edge $e \in E$ has an ordered pair of endpoints $(s(e), t(e)) \in V \times V$, with segment $[e] = [\iota(s(e)), \iota(t(e))]$;…
nodes.title: Euler's polyhedron formula

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a finite set of subsets of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ such that every member of $T$ is the convex hull of three points $a, b, c$ of the plane (not necessarily distinct), the union of the members of $T$ is the closed unit square $[0,1]^2$, any two distinct members of $T$ have disjoint interiors, and all members of $T$ have the same Lebesgue measure. Then the number of members of $T$ is even.
nodes.title: Monsky's theorem

nodes.summary: There are an integer $n > 1$ and real numbers $x_i$, $y_i$ and $s_i > 0$ for $i = 1, \dots, n$, with the $s_i$ pairwise distinct, such that the union of the closed squares $[x_i, x_i + s_i] \times [y_i, y_i + s_i]$ is the unit square $[0, 1] \times [0, 1]$ and any two of these squares with different indices have disjoint interiors.
nodes.title: Squaring the square with distinct squares

nodes.summary: Every finite non-collinear subset of the real Euclidean plane determines an ordinary line: two points of the set such that no third point of the set is collinear with them.
nodes.title: Sylvester–Gallai theorem
